text:
alex: Heads up — manager-level reports are missing rows for parts of Acme Corp after yesterday's retention change. Several teams reported managers seeing zero activity for February despite events in raw logs. Anyone else?

sam: Saw the ticket, can you paste repro steps and a quick curl/SQL so I can try locally? @maria FYI for analytics.

alex: Repro steps: query the usage endpoint with role=manager and a recent range — returns empty array. curl example: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/analytics/usage?org=acme&role=manager&from=1700000000&to=1710000000'``` Response: 200 OK, body: `[]`. Note: non-manager roles return normal rows.

maria: Interesting — last night we ran the ttl-migration to standardize retention windows for linked accounts (set default 30d). @jamie can you check if the migration wrote anything odd for Acme?

jamie: Pulling audit logs now — I see a migration job that wrote `ttl_days=0` for linked_org_id=`acme-child-2` at 2026-03-12T03:14Z. That's suspicious. If TTL=0 our aggregation cleanup treats the data as expired and prunes aggregates. Can you confirm which org IDs are missing?

alex: Affected: `acme-child-2` and `acme-sales` show manager-level rows missing. `acme-parent` and `acme-child-1` look OK. Engineers' rows are intact for all orgs.

sam: That pattern (only manager-role rows gone) could be caused by role-level aggregates being stored with org-scoped TTL metadata. Quick check — run on analytics-prod: ```SELECT org_id, role, count(*) FROM aggregates WHERE org_id IN ('acme-child-2','acme-sales') AND timestamp >= '2026-02-01' GROUP BY org_id, role;```

maria: Ran that against a read replica — role='manager' counts are zero, while role='engineer' has normal counts. Raw events exist in `events` table, so ingestion didn't drop. Looks like the rollup/aggregator cleanup pruned the aggregated rows due to TTL evaluation.

jamie: Root cause hypothesis: the migration script didn't handle nil/defaults correctly and wrote ttl_days=0 for some linked_org records. Our cleanup job treats ttl<=0 as immediate expiry, which deleted historical aggregates for role-level keys.

alex: Customer is on Dedicated and this is an SLA-impacting issue. They want ETA and a mitigation path.

sam: Immediate mitigation: (1) revert the bad TTL writes to previous values, (2) re-run targeted historical rollup/backfill for affected orgs with `ignore_ttl=true`. Jamie, can you queue that?

jamie: I'll queue a targeted backfill for `acme-child-2` and `acme-sales` now with ignore_ttl. ETA ~2 hours for initial results. Also deploying a hotfix to prevent ttl=0 writes.

maria: We should also add an alert to detect sudden aggregate drops by org+role (e.g., >75% decrease in 1h) and send to eng-oncall. That would have caught this faster.

sam: I'll draft the customer update: brief root cause, actions taken (reverted TTL, backfill queued, patch merged) and ETA for full restoration once backfill completes.

jamie: Hotfix pushed to migration service, prevents writing ttl_days<1 and adds a preflight check. Backfill started at 2026-03-13T12:20Z. I'll post logs when it's done.

support-bot: Incident updated: INC-2026-314. Backfill initiated for acme-child-2 and acme-sales. Monitor: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026-314

alex: Thanks — please tag me when backfill completes so I can confirm manager views in the console. I'll include the interim note to the customer.
